domain: Political Philosophy / International Law / Migration Studies
topic_summary: Analysis of the border control kernel as contested between sovereignty-primary and freedom-of-movement-primary readings. Each reading instantiates a different constraint with distinct victim sets: excluded migrants under sovereignty-primary borders vs displaced domestic workers under freedom-of-movement-primary borders. The kernel is the normative status of territorial boundaries in regulating human movement.

key_entities: UN Charter (establishes state sovereignty over borders)
UDHR Article 13.1 (right to freedom of movement within states, not between)
Excluded migrants (those barred from crossing borders)
Domestic workers (native labor force affected by migration)
Human rights advocates (promote individual liberty of movement)
key_tensions: Individual rights vs state sovereignty (core structural opposition)
Right to emigrate vs no right to immigrate (legal asymmetry)
Border control as security vs border control as rights violation

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The normative status of territorial boundaries as legitimate regulators of human movement across space
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: State sovereignty doctrine (Westphalian system) vs cosmopolitan human rights framework; interpretive legitimacy contested between state actors and international human rights institutions

readings.commitment: Territorial boundaries are legitimate instruments of collective self-determination; states have foundational authority to exclude non-members
readings.authority_grounding: Westphalian sovereignty doctrine; UN Charter Article 2(1); national security framework
readings.expected_structural_delta: Excluded migrants enter victim set; border enforcement becomes legitimate state function; displacement of citizens treated as externality or non-issue

readings.commitment: Freedom of movement is a fundamental human right that borders impermissibly restrict; exclusion requires extraordinary justification
readings.authority_grounding: Cosmopolitan moral philosophy; extension of UDHR Article 13.1 logic across borders; individual autonomy primacy
readings.expected_structural_delta: Excluded migrants exit victim set (no legitimate exclusion); displaced domestic workers enter victim set; border enforcement becomes rights violation requiring justification

readings.commitment: States retain border control authority but must exercise it proportionately to legitimate state interests and consistently with human rights obligations
readings.authority_grounding: International human rights law synthesis; proportionality doctrine; refugee convention obligations
readings.expected_structural_delta: Both excluded migrants and displaced citizens in victim set; border control legitimate only when justified, necessary, proportionate; creates adjudication burden on states

axiom_contradictions.basis: Sovereignty-primary holds that states have foundational authority to exclude (exclusion requires no justification beyond state decision); freedom-primary holds that exclusion is a rights violation requiring extraordinary justification. No single framework can hold both: either exclusion is presumptively legitimate or presumptively illegitimate.

axes.structural_delta: Borders as legitimate instruments of collective self-determination with foundational exclusion authority
axes.primary_observable: Legal doctrine treating border control as core sovereignty function; policy requiring no justification for exclusion beyond state decision
axes.selection_reason: First reading of contested kernel; distinct victim set (excluded migrants); high epsilon from enforcement apparatus

axes.structural_delta: Borders as impermissible restrictions on fundamental human right to movement requiring extraordinary justification
axes.primary_observable: Moral/legal framework treating exclusion as rights violation; policy requiring justification for any border enforcement
axes.selection_reason: Second reading of contested kernel; inverted victim set from sovereignty_primary; axiom-contradictory to first reading

axes.structural_delta: Border control authority constrained by proportionality and human rights obligations
axes.primary_observable: Proportionality tests in border enforcement; refugee convention compliance; human rights adjudication of exclusion decisions
axes.selection_reason: Third reading of contested kernel; synthesis position attempting to hold both victim sets; demonstrates structural impossibility of full reconciliation

axes.structural_delta: Migration's differential impact on native workers by skill level and sector
axes.primary_observable: Wage effects and employment displacement by education level; occupational downgrading patterns
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: empirical mechanism feeding into sovereignty_primary reading but lower structural priority than kernel readings themselves

axes.structural_delta: International law grants emigration rights but no corresponding immigration rights
axes.primary_observable: UDHR Article 13.1 scope; absence of reciprocal entry rights in international law
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: legal structure supporting sovereignty_primary but captured by that reading's constraint story

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Migration's differential impact on native workers by skill level
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Empirical mechanism feeding sovereignty_primary reading; lower structural priority than kernel readings; captured in sovereignty_primary constraint story as affects_constraint hook

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Right to emigrate without corresponding right to immigrate
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Legal structure supporting sovereignty_primary reading; fully captured by that reading's constraint story; no independent epsilon

omegas.description: Refugee Convention creates partial exception to sovereignty_primary reading (non-refoulement obligation). Does this exception prove the rule or undermine it? If states can be obligated to admit some non-citizens, sovereignty_primary's foundational exclusion authority is already compromised.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) — refugee law conspicuously absent from sovereignty_primary framing

omegas.description: All three readings treat citizenship as given (accident of birth). None address whether citizenship acquisition rules themselves are legitimate constraints. If birthright citizenship is arbitrary, sovereignty_primary's beneficiary set (citizens) may itself be a Snare.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) — who benefits from citizenship-as-given framing

omegas.description: Does qualified_sovereignty reading collapse into one of the other two under pressure? If proportionality review is deferential (state wins most cases), it collapses to sovereignty_primary. If proportionality review is strict (exclusion rarely justified), it collapses to freedom_primary. The synthesis may be unstable.
omegas.source: Independence testing — qualified_sovereignty may not have independent epsilon from its parent readings

omegas.description: Labor market displacement evidence is mixed (Brazil +3% wages, Colombia -30% for low-education workers). Is this a Mountain (economic mechanism) or a Piton (policy choice to protect/not protect domestic workers)? Classification affects whether displacement is inevitable or contingent.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel decomposition successful: three readings with distinct victim sets and axiom contradictions identified. Labor market displacement deferred as empirical mechanism rather than independent reading.
